# Self-Discipline and Goals

A consistent, intense streak of self-improvement runs through [[Traveler Stansberry]]'s private notes — recurring challenge regimens and rules he sets for himself.

## The regimens

### 75 Hard / 75 Medium
Two versions of an extended self-discipline challenge. Sources: [[sources/75 hard 2025]] and [[sources/75 medium]].

**75 Medium rules** (from [[sources/75 medium]], exact):
- Work out 5 days a week
- No porn
- No smoking / no vaping / no drinking
- Read 30 minutes daily
- Lock in for SAT
- < 3 hours of screen time
- Eat well, > 1,500 calories/day, 100 g protein

**75 Hard** (from [[sources/75 hard 2025]]): stricter variant; also bans weed and carries the "if I cannot do this, I am generationally cooked forever… consistency is key" language. The tone is unsparing and maximalist.

**Comparison:** 75 Medium is materially the same as 75 Hard on abstinence (no nicotine, alcohol, porn) but softens intensity, drops the explicit weed prohibition, and adds a concrete SAT prep goal — suggesting it was written during a test-prep window (likely 2024–25, see [[College Search]]). The nutrition floor (>1,500 cal, 100 g protein) points to a body-composition goal alongside performance goals.

### Lock In
Daily operating rules: homework before anything, no nicotine, pushups, sleep by 10:30, no weekday hangouts. Source: [[sources/lock in]].

### Opposite Action
References a DBT-style coping skill ("opposite action") and a "dave session" — structured work on emotional self-management. *(Sensitive; recorded plainly.)* Source: [[sources/opposite action]].

## What it reveals

A high-achieving, self-demanding temperament with a clear habit of **externalizing willpower into rule systems**. This dovetails with his intellectual claim that *"strong is using willpower to overcome deterministic… tendencies"* (see [[Fate and Free Will]] and [[Intellectual Interests]]): the self-discipline isn't merely habit formation — it's his *lived answer* to the free-will question he keeps testing in literature.

The SAT flag in 75 Medium is the most concrete academic-prep signal in any of the challenge notes; it suggests these regimens aren't abstract self-help but tied to specific high-stakes outcomes.

> [!warning] Gap: no evidence of completion
> None of the challenge notes records outcomes, streaks, or compliance data. Whether Traveler completed any iteration of 75 Hard or 75 Medium is unknown. The *intention* is clearly documented; the *follow-through* is not.

## See also

[[Traveler Stansberry]] · [[Family and Personal Life]] · [[Fate and Free Will]] · [[College Search]] · [[Academic Record]]

# Homework Hatch (startup)

[[Traveler Stansberry]]'s real edtech/AI venture (2025), variously called **Homework Hatch**, **SPHW Buddy**, and **HW Buddy** — the concrete, real-world version of the AI ambition he keeps circling in his fiction.

## The product
An AI study platform that ingests a student's **LMS data** (Canvas, Schoology) and turns it into:
- AI study plans, summaries, practice quizzes (Kahoot/Gimkit-style), a class-focused chatbot
- A **college-acceptance-% calculator**, recommendations, test prep
- A gamified "**Buddy Coins**" arcade economy (coins earned by completing assignments)
- Class/grade/club chats

### College acceptance calculator — metric definition
From [[Homework Hatch Stuff (apple note)]]:

> **Out-of-state acceptance rate formula:** `# out-of-state acceptances / total # of applicants`

> [!warning] Denominator ambiguity
> The standard out-of-state acceptance rate uses **out-of-state applicants** as the denominator. This note uses **total applicants** instead, which yields a smaller, non-standard figure. Unclear if intentional (e.g. "what share of our whole user pool are out-of-state admits") or a first-draft approximation. Should be clarified before the feature ships.

## Business thinking ([[prices]], [[idea]])
Three tiers — Normal $10 / Premium $20 / Pro $25 — with AI cost modeled at ~$2–3/user and hosting ~$2/user. The [[idea]] note includes a full ChatGPT-assisted pricing & break-even analysis (e.g. the "premium trap" problem). Tech stack surfaced in his notes: **AWS** (Elastic Beanstalk), **GitHub Actions**, **Playwright** (automated LMS login w/ 2FA handling), **Stripe**, iOS App Store release.

> [!warning] Security
> An associated note held **live AWS credentials in plaintext** and was deleted during ingest; those keys should be rotated. (Logged in [[log]].)

## Building it for real — the ChatGPT build log (2025–26)
His ChatGPT export (51+ chats) turns Homework Hatch from a plan into a documented build. He shipped it largely by **"vibe coding" in [[Cursor (AI code editor)|Cursor]]**, then deliberately set out to *actually* learn to code so he could understand and edit his own app ([[Learning to Code for Homework Hatch - Beyond Vibe Coding (chat)]]).
- **Stack & deploy:** a **Flask** backend on **AWS**, evolving from **Elastic Beanstalk** → **App Runner + ECR** (he hit a 12 GB Docker-image wall), with **GitHub Actions** CI/CD, IAM keys, content filtering, and WebSocket config ([[Deploying a Flask App - AWS Elastic Beanstalk, GitHub Actions, and IAM Keys (chat)]], [[Fixing the Docker-to-ECR Push Failure for Homework Hatch - App Runner and the 12GB Image (chat)]], [[Launch to AWS Elastic Beanstalk - Flask Deploy and WebSocket Config (chat)]]). He repeatedly uploaded full codebase zips for architecture reviews ([[HW Buddy App Architecture Analysis and GPT-5 Model Choice (chat)]]).
- **Co-founder [[Josh (Homework Hatch co-founder)|Josh]]:** he walked through granting Josh AWS Identity Center access screen-by-screen ([[AWS Identity Center Setup for Homework Hatch and Wikipedia Training Dataset (chat)]]).
- **LMS ingestion — the pivot:** the plan relied on the **Canvas API**, but his school **revoked the API key**, forcing a pivot to a browser-extension scraper and cloud-storage OAuth (Google Drive / Microsoft OneDrive), where he ran into the OAuth consent-screen wall ([[Canvas API Key Revoked - Extension Scraper and LMS Access Strategy (chat)]], [[OneDrive Azure Integration and the OAuth Consent Wall for Homework Hatch (chat)]], [[Google Drive Folder Tree Mirroring for Homework Hatch (chat)]]).
- **n8n automation ("Anna"):** an "AI secretary" built in **[[n8n (automation platform)|n8n]]** — a Telegram voice note → Google Calendar assistant (chronic date-drift bug), a command router across Telegram/Calendar/Instagram, plus Instagram marketing automation ([[n8n Command Router for Homework Hatch - Telegram, Calendar, Instagram (chat)]], [[n8n Debugging - Google Calendar Voice Assistant for Homework Hatch (chat)]]). Also a prototype Discord bot on the OpenAI API.
- **Incorporated:** filed as a **Maryland LLC** (Sept 2025) — Articles of Organization, EIN, domain transfer, Stripe ([[Filing the Maryland LLC for Homework Hatch - Articles, EIN, and Stripe (chat)]]).
- **Business & launch:** valuation + AWS unit-cost modeling, GPT-5 model selection, a study-materials spec (flashcards, live quiz, practice banks) written as Cursor prompts, and a pre-launch **competitor strategy with an "admin-free privacy pivot"** ~2 weeks before launch ([[Homework Hatch Competitor Strategy and the Admin-Free Privacy Pivot (chat)]], [[Study Materials Spec for Homework Hatch - Flashcards, Live Quiz, Practice Banks (chat)]]).

# Economics IA

SL Economics IA — a portfolio of **three article commentaries** across the syllabus (Mr. Erickson).

---

## The three commentaries

### 1. Microeconomics — "Change" *(most detailed; original topic statement preserved below)*
- **Research question:** *How will the changes from Grand Theft Auto 5 to Grand Theft Auto 6 affect the total revenue Rockstar Games generates in 2025?*
- **Framework:** supply-and-demand shift analysis; the product change (GTA 5 → GTA 6) as the demand-side event.
- **Key figures:** projected ~$3 billion first-year sales; $100 price point (premium tier).
- **Company focus:** [[Rockstar Games]] / Take-Two Interactive as the firm; total revenue as the dependent variable.
- **Topic rationale (in his own words):** "GTA 6 has been a long awaited video game, following the success of its predecessor GTA 5. There have been many speculations on the future popularity of the game, and I hope to dive deep and figure out how big this game is and how the public will receive it." — the topic choice sits at the intersection of his [[Gaming and PC Setup|gaming interest]] and his economics coursework.
- **Significance:** demonstrates ability to apply micro theory (demand shifts, revenue analysis) to a real, consumer-market event he personally follows.

> [!note] Timing note
> The micro IA was produced in **2025** (Year 1 / 11th grade), before GTA 6's launch date was confirmed. Projections were speculative-market estimates, not outturn data. Whether the actual 2025 revenue figures were retroactively compared is not documented in the sources.

### 2. Macroeconomics — "Economic well-being"
Japan's zero/negative interest-rate policy (BoJ, 1999 & 2016 interventions); AD/AS analysis explaining why an aging population and near-zero birthrate keep LRAS flat → inflation-without-growth. Topic chosen partly for his 12-year Japanese-language study ([[IB Japanese (SL)]]).

### 3. International — "Intervention"
Argentina / Milei's crawling-peg FX reform; real vs. nominal depreciation, balance of payments, export competitiveness.

---

## Thematic coherence across the three
The portfolio spans all three syllabus sections (micro / macro / international) with a unifying thread: **how does a major change — in a market, in monetary policy, in exchange-rate regime — shift equilibrium and affect a key economic actor?** The micro piece makes that logic explicit in its title keyword "Change."

## Why it matters
Together the three commentaries demonstrate command of:
- Demand-supply diagramming and revenue analysis (micro)
- Monetary policy mechanics and AD-AS modeling (macro)
- Exchange-rate theory and balance-of-payments (international)

These are the analytical foundations of his [[College Search|finance direction]] and [[Investment Club]] leadership. Combined with his [[Extended Essay (Economics)|EE]] on COVID-era fiscal policy and inflation, the IB economics record is one of his most substantive academic outputs.
